description: The bookkeeping that stops the checklist becoming a survey. These gates answer to the run's own state rather than to an attestation, so the run cannot close by claiming it is finished.

gates.title: The Run Was Opened Before The Work
gates.rule: A run exists and the changes are recorded against it. Work done outside a run is work nothing checked, and an unchecked change looks exactly like a passing one afterwards.

gates.title: A Baseline Was Measured Before The First Edit
gates.rule: The run holds a measurement taken before anything changed. Without one there is no way to tell an improvement from a regression, and every later number is a claim rather than a comparison.
gates.fix: scripts/psi.py measure --url <live url> --label before, or scripts/lighthouse.py measure --url <preview url> --label before

gates.title: Scope Is Every Route, Not The One Named
gates.rule: The targets cover every route the site serves, not only the page the prompt mentioned. A bundle split on one route and left whole on nine others has not been split.
gates.fix: Widen the targets with scan --target, or answer n/a naming why those routes are outside this deliverable.

gates.title: Every File In Scope Was Read And Ruled On
gates.rule: Each file under the targets ends either changed or explicitly ruled as needing no performance change, with the reason. A file nobody opened and a file considered and left alone are indistinguishable without this.
gates.fix: perf-pass.py files, then read each one and either change it or file-clear it with a note.

gates.title: Every Applicable Gate Is Answered
gates.rule: No gate is left silent. A gate that is not met is work to do; the only ways past one are changing the project or naming the condition that puts it out of scope.
gates.fix: perf-pass.py status lists what is open.

gates.title: The Filled Checklist Was Rendered
gates.rule: The run ends with the whole checklist shown - every gate, its verdict, the evidence, the before and after numbers, and a section listing anything answered not applicable and why.
